recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 784: May 5, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 784 covers Node.js 26.0.0 release with Temporal API enabled by default, V8 14.6, and Undici 8. Notable releases include PM2 7.0, Astro v7 Alpha (Vite 8 + Rust compiler), Electron 41.5, ESLint 10.3, and Zod 4.4. Featured articles include testing Vue components in the browser, Mozilla's WAICT spec for cryptographically verifying JavaScript integrity in Firefox Nightly, a story about cutting a $134 Cloudflare D1 bill by 95%, and concerns about Anthropic acquiring Bun. Also highlighted: opentype.js for font manipulation, pnpm v11.0.5, Cloudflare open-sourcing Agentic Inbox, and the Ladybird independent browser project's latest JS/CSS improvements.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 783: April 28, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 783 curates the latest in the JS ecosystem. Highlights include a comprehensive overview of ES2025 and ES2026 features (iterator helpers, Promise.try, Map.getOrInsert, Temporal), a new JS package manager called Aube focused on performance, Nano Stores 1.3 (a 286-byte framework-agnostic state manager), tips on debugging WASM in Chrome DevTools, writing Node.js addons with .NET Native AOT, and a guide on the simplest C-to-WebAssembly-to-JS pipeline. Also covered: Cloudflare agent-readiness tools, Cypress TypeScript 6.0 upgrade, and miscellaneous ecosystem news.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 782: April 21, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 782 covers a range of ecosystem news and releases. Key highlights include Node.js 24.15.0 LTS stabilizing require(esm) and the module compile cache, Bun v1.3.13 adding test isolation, parallelization, sharding, and 5% memory reduction, and Fable 5.0 adding .NET 10 and F# 10 support. A senior Microsoft engineer shares how they resolved 15,000 circular dependencies in a 7-million-line TypeScript monorepo. There's also an opinion piece advocating for domain-first vertical codebase structure over type-based folder organization, the OWASP NPM security best practices cheat sheet, Git 2.54 release notes, and a Cloudflare CLI preview.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 781: April 14, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 781 covers MDN's frontend rebuild ditching React in favor of web components and a custom server component system, Expo's mobile development workflow for JS developers, and an entertaining exploration of the Firefox extension ecosystem. Release highlights include Mantine 9.0 with calendar scheduling components, wa-sqlite 1.1 (WebAssembly SQLite for browsers), gridstack.js 12.6, Formula.js 4.6, and Lexical 0.43. Also featured: Windows 95 as an Electron app (v5.0) with folder mounting, ISO support, and improved internet access.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 780: April 7, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 780 covers Google open-sourcing JSIR, a high-level intermediate representation for JavaScript aimed at enabling better tooling like linters and bundlers. Also featured: a 2026 JavaScript landscape overview by Chris Coyier, a piece on using minimum package release age as a supply chain defense, and an exploration of modern CSS capabilities replacing JavaScript for UI tasks. Releases include ESLint v10.2.0 with language-aware rules, Node.js 25.9.0 with a new iterable streams API, npm-check-updates v20, and several Vue 3 libraries.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 779: March 31, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 779 covers a supply chain security incident with advice on pinning dependencies and using cooldowns for updates. Notable releases include Inertia.js 3.0, Node.js security patches across multiple LTS versions, TanStack DB 0.6 with persistence and offline support, Astro 6.1, Mantine 9.0, and Knip v6 with 2-4x performance gains via oxc integration. Featured articles include an explanation of the push-pull algorithm behind signals in frameworks like Solid, Vue, and Angular; a decompilation of the White House's React Native app revealing security concerns; and a case study on replacing Node.js with Bun for 5x throughput. Also highlighted is Pretext, a multiline text measurement library that went viral with 22M impressions and 25k GitHub stars.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 778: March 24, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 778 covers the TypeScript 6.0 release, which bridges the gap to the upcoming Go-powered TypeScript 7.0 compiler. Key changes include strict mode on by default, ESNext module defaults, deprecation of ES5 targets and AMD/UMD/SystemJS output, and a new --stableTypeOrdering flag. Other highlights: Next.js 16.2 with faster startup and rendering, pnpm 11 Beta moving to a SQLite-powered store, a React SSR framework performance benchmark comparing TanStack Start, React Router, and Next.js, an analysis of JavaScript bundle bloat causes, Node.js security releases addressing nine vulnerabilities, Deno employee departures, and a Node.js community debate over LLM-generated code contributions.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 777: March 17, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 777 covers Vite 8.0's major release featuring Rolldown replacing Rollup/esbuild, Babel-free React plugin, Wasm SSR support, and big performance gains. VoidZero open-sourced its Vite+ unified toolchain (now in alpha). Other highlights include Electron 41.0, Vitest 4.1, Nuxt 4.4, Babel 8.0 RC3, and Vue 3.6.0 Beta 8. Featured articles cover source maps becoming an ECMA standard, a team rewriting 130K lines from React to Svelte in two weeks using LLMs, and an empirical study of frontend memory leaks across 500 React, Vue, and Angular apps.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 776: March 10, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 776 covers several notable items: Solid 2.0 Beta launches with first-class async support, replacing Suspense with a Loading component and adding an action() primitive for mutations. TypeScript 6.0 RC is out as a stepping stone toward the Go-powered TypeScript 7.0. Patreon shares a retrospective on migrating 11,000 files (1M lines) to TypeScript over seven years. A JavaScript worm accidentally triggered on Wikipedia vandalized ~4,000 Meta-Wiki pages. ArkType 2.2 adds runtime-validated functions via type.fn. Also covered: JSLinux now supports x86_64/AVX-512/APX, a URL quirk with newline/tab characters, compiling Node.js on Jetson Nano, and recreating Flappy Bird in pure CSS.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Weekly Issue 775: March 3, 2026
recent_posts.summary: JavaScript Weekly issue 775 covers Bun v1.3.10 with a rewritten REPL, browser compile target for self-contained HTML apps, TC39 stage 3 ES decorators support, and performance improvements. Also featured: an argument for a better Web Streams API addressing usability and performance flaws, an explanation of why JavaScript-only DRM is ineffective, plus minor releases for React PDF 10.4, JSNES 2.0, Milkdown 7.19, and Peggy 5.1.
